stages.title: Reading and writing fundamentals
explain: Italian spelling is regular, but some groups make special sounds. "gn" sounds like Spanish ñ (gnocchi), "gli" sounds like "lli" in "million" (famiglia), and "sc" before e or i sounds like "sh" (scena, pesce).

Before a, o and u, "c" and "g" are hard (casa, gatto). Before e and i they are soft (cena, gelato). Add h to keep them hard: "chi", "che", "ghe", "ghi". Days and months are written with small letters: "lunedì", "marzo".

gq.why: The group gn makes one palatal nasal sound.

gq.q: Why is there an h in "chiesa"?
o: It keeps the c hard before i
gq.why: The h stops c from becoming soft "ch" before e or i.

panel.q: How is "cena" (dinner) pronounced?
panel.why: C is soft before e.

panel.q: Which spelling is correct for the sound of "key"?
panel.why: Chi is written with ch to keep the c hard.

panel.q: A learner says "kasa" for "casa". Why does Italian not spell it with k?
o: K is not part of the native alphabet; c before a is already hard
panel.why: Native Italian words use c for the k sound before a, o, u.

points.ask: When are c and g soft?

teach.model: Italian spelling is regular. Special groups are gn, gli and sc. C and g are hard before a, o and u and soft before e and i. Add h to keep them hard.

stages.hook: Read "gnocchi" and "scuola" aloud. Which letter groups make new sounds?
stages.mnemonic: C and G go soft with E and I; add H to keep them hard.

stages.title: Basic sentence construction
explain: The basic order is subject, verb, object: "Marco mangia una mela". The subject pronoun is often dropped because the verb ending shows the person: "Mangio" means "I eat". Adjectives usually follow the noun: "una macchina rossa". Some, like bello and grande, can come before.
To make a sentence negative, put "non" before the verb: "Non mangio la carne". The double negative is normal: "Non vedo niente" means "I see nothing".

gq.why: Non goes directly before the verb.

gq.q: Why does "Non vedo niente" mean "I see nothing" and not "I see something"?
gq.why: Non and niente together form one negation.

panel.q: Why can Italians say "Parlo italiano" without "io"?
o: The verb ending marks the subject
panel.why: Each person has its own ending.

panel.q: When might you keep the pronoun, as in "Io mangio, tu no"?
o: To contrast or stress the subject
panel.why: Pronouns are used for emphasis and contrast.

panel.q: A learner says "Mangio non la carne". What is wrong?
o: Non must come before the verb
panel.why: Italian puts non before the conjugated verb.

teach.model: An Italian sentence goes subject, verb, object. The subject pronoun is often dropped because the verb ending shows the person. For no, put non before the verb.

stages.hook: In Italian you can say "Ho fame" without saying "io". How is a basic sentence built?
stages.mnemonic: Non goes before the verb, never after.

stages.title: Common verbs
explain: The key verbs are irregular. Essere: sono, sei, è, siamo, siete, sono. Avere: ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno. Andare (to go): vado, vai, va, andiamo, andate, vanno. Fare (to do, make): faccio, fai, fa, facciamo, fate, fanno.
Use "stare" for how you are: "Sto bene". Use "stare per + infinitive" for something about to happen: "Sto per mangiare" means I am about to eat.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: Noi ___ a Roma.
Why does "sono" mean both "I am" and "they are"?
o: Essere has the same form for io and loro
gq.why: In the present, io and loro share the form sono.

panel.q: What is the difference between "ho" and "hanno"?
o: Ho is I have; hanno is they have
panel.why: Both are forms of avere.

panel.q: In "Come stai? Sto bene" which verb is used?
panel.why: Stare is used for state and health.

panel.q: Why are the most common verbs irregular?
o: They are used so often that they kept old forms
panel.why: Frequent words resist regularisation.

points.ask: How do I say how I am?

teach.model: Essere means to be, avere to have, andare to go and fare to do. They are irregular, so learn each form. For example sono, ho, vado, faccio.

stages.hook: In Italian "I am" is "sono" and "I have" is "ho". What do the most common verbs look like?
stages.mnemonic: Essere, avere, andare, fare: your four big helpers.

stages.title: Nouns, pronouns and modifiers
explain: Use il for masculine singular, la for feminine singular, l' before a vowel. Use lo before s plus consonant or z, such as "lo studente" and "lo zio". The plurals are i, gli (before vowels, z, s plus consonant) and le.

Plurals change the ending: -o becomes -i, -a becomes -e, -e becomes -i. Some nouns end in -co or -go and change spelling: amico becomes amici. Possessives agree with the noun: "il mio libro", "la mia casa", "i miei amici".

gq.q: What is the plural of "lo studente"?
Why is it "il mio libro" with an article?
o: Italian uses the article with possessives except for singular relatives
gq.why: The article is normal with mio, mia, etc.

panel.q: What is the plural of "amico"?
panel.why: Amico takes -ci in the plural; the feminine plural amiche keeps the h to stay hard.

panel.q: Why is it "gli amici" and not "i amici"?
o: Gli is used before a vowel
panel.why: Masculine plural uses gli before a vowel.

panel.q: A learner says "la zio". What is wrong?
o: Zio is masculine and takes lo
panel.why: Zio is a masculine noun starting with z.

points.ask: How do I make a plural?

teach.model: Use il or lo for masculine, la for feminine and l' before a vowel. Plurals are i or gli for masculine and le for feminine. Possessives agree with the noun, like il mio libro.

stages.hook: Italian has several words for "the": il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le. How do you pick the right one?
stages.mnemonic: Il and i; la and le; lo and gli.

stages.title: Questions and responses
explain: Usually it does not. You raise the voice at the end: "Parli italiano?" To ask for information use a question word: chi (who), che cosa (what), dove (where), quando (when), perché (why), come (how), quanto (how much).

"Perché" means both "why" and "because". To answer yes use "sì", to answer no use "no". Note "Dov'è la stazione?" means where is the station. For polite questions to strangers use Lei: "Scusi, dov'è la banca?"
sentences: How much does it cost, please?

gq.q: How do you turn "Parli italiano" into a question?
o: Raise your voice at the end
Move the verb to the end
gq.why: Italian questions often keep statement order.

o: It means both why and because

panel.q: Which question word fits "Quando arriva il treno?"
panel.why: Quando means when.

panel.q: Why is "Scusi" better than "Scusa" for a stranger?
o: Scusi is the polite Lei form
panel.why: Lei is used with strangers and elders.

panel.q: Why is there an apostrophe in "Dov'è"?
o: Dove drops its e before è
panel.why: Elision joins dove and è.

points.ask: How do I ask a simple question?

teach.model: In Italian a question can have the same order as a statement with a rising voice. Use chi, dove, quando, perché, come and quanto to ask for information. Perché means both why and because.

stages.hook: How do you ask a question in Italian? Does the word order change?
stages.mnemonic: Perché asks and answers: why, because.

stages.title: Describing people and places
explain: Adjectives agree with the noun. Those in -o have four forms: alto, alta, alti, alte. Those in -e have two: grande (singular) and grandi (plural). Adjectives usually follow the noun, but bello, buono and grande can come before it.
To say what is in a place use "c'è" (there is) and "ci sono" (there are): "C'è un parco vicino a casa". "Vicino a" means near and "lontano da" means far from.
sentences: There is a park near here.

gq.q: Choose the correct form: La ragazza è ___
Why does "gentile" not change for feminine?
o: Adjectives in -e have one singular form
gq.why: Adjectives in -e change only for the plural.

panel.q: What is the plural of "grande"?
panel.why: Adjectives in -e form the plural in -i.

panel.q: Why is "un bel parco" correct?
o: Bello shortens before a masculine noun
panel.why: Bello becomes bel before consonants.

panel.q: What is the difference between "c'è" and "ci sono"?
panel.why: C'è is there is and ci sono is there are.

points.ask: How do I describe a place?

teach.model: Adjectives agree with the noun in Italian. Those in -o have four forms: alto, alta, alti, alte. Those in -e have two forms. Use c'è and ci sono to say what is in a place.

stages.hook: How do you describe a tall girl and a tall boy? Does "alto" change?

stages.title: Time, dates and daily routines
explain: To ask the time say "Che ore sono?" For 1 o'clock say "È l'una" and for others "Sono le tre". Say "e mezza" for half past, "e un quarto" for quarter past and "meno un quarto" for quarter to. Midday is mezzogiorno.

Days: lunedì, martedì, mercoledì, giovedì, venerdì, sabato, domenica. A date is "il 5 maggio" and the first is "il primo maggio". Reflexive verbs show routines: "mi sveglio" (I wake up), "mi alzo" (I get up).

gq.q: How do you say "It is one o'clock"?
Why is it "Sono le tre" but "È l'una"?
o: Una is singular while tre is plural
gq.why: The verb agrees with the number of hours.

panel.q: What does "mi alzo" show?
panel.why: Reflexive verbs use a pronoun like mi.

panel.q: What does "Sono le tre e mezza" mean?
o: It is a quarter to three
panel.why: E mezza means half past.

panel.q: Why is Sunday "domenica" a feminine noun while Monday is masculine?
o: Only Sunday ends in -a and is feminine
panel.why: Domenica is feminine; other days are masculine.

points.ask: How do I ask the time?
How do I say I get up?

teach.model: Ask Che ore sono? Answer È l'una or Sono le due. Add e mezza or e un quarto. Reflexive verbs show routines, such as mi alzo.

sources: Date and time notation in Europe
stages.hook: What time is it? How do you give a date in Italian?
stages.mnemonic: È l'una, sono le due: one is singular, the rest plural.

stages.title: Food and shopping
explain: Say "Vorrei un caffè, per favore." Vorrei is a polite way to say I would like. Ask the price with "Quanto costa?" or "Quanto fa?" In many busy bars, people pay first at the cassa, then show the receipt at the counter.

Use the partitive "del, della, dei" for an unspecified quantity: "Mangio del pane". After quantities use di: "un chilo di mele". Shops include la panetteria, la macelleria and il mercato. Italy uses the euro.

gq.q: Which is the polite way to order?
Why is it "un chilo di mele" and not "un chilo delle mele"?
o: After a quantity di alone is used

panel.q: In a shop, which greeting is expected?
panel.why: A courteous greeting on entering is normal.

panel.q: Why does "del pane" differ from English "bread"?
o: Italian often uses the partitive for some
panel.why: The partitive means "some".

panel.q: Why do Italians often drink espresso standing at the bar?
o: It is a quick everyday ritual, and the counter price is often lower
panel.why: Standing at the bar is customary, and sitting at a table often costs more.

points.ask: How do I ask the price?
How do I say some bread?

teach.model: In a shop say Buongiorno. Order with Vorrei and ask Quanto costa? Use del, della or dei for some of something. After quantities use di.

stages.hook: You are in an Italian bar. How do you order a coffee and pay?
stages.mnemonic: Vorrei is the magic word for polite orders.

stages.title: Everyday conversations
explain: A typical chat starts with a greeting, then "Come va?" or "Come stai?" The answer can be "Bene, grazie", "Non c'è male" or "Così così". Then ask back with "E tu?"
To make a plan say "Andiamo?" and "D'accordo" or "Va bene". To end say "A presto" (see you soon), "A domani" (see you tomorrow) or "Buona giornata".
sentences: I am sorry, I am late.

gq.q: A friend asks "Come stai?" What is a good reply?
gq.why: The reply plus a question keeps the chat going.

gq.q: Why use "E tu?" with a friend and "E Lei?" with a stranger?
o: It matches informal or formal address

panel.q: What does "Va bene" show?
panel.why: Va bene means OK.

panel.q: Why say "A presto" when leaving?
o: It expresses hope to meet again soon
panel.why: It is a friendly closing.

panel.q: What makes an Italian conversation sound polite?
o: Greeting first, using Lei when needed, and thanking
panel.why: Polite rituals and the right form of address matter.

teach.model: Start with Ciao or Buongiorno. Ask Come stai? and answer Bene, grazie. Ask back with E tu? To close say A presto or Buona giornata.

stages.hook: Two friends meet on the street. What might they say to each other?
stages.mnemonic: Come va? Va bene! E tu? is the first dance of any chat.
